reference: F. Poletti and P. Horak, 'Description of ultrashort pulse propagation in multimode optical fibers', J. Opt. Soc. Am. B 25, 1645 (2008)
description: The extended (multimode) GNLSE itself. Section 4 analyses the symmetry properties of the four-mode nonlinear coupling coefficients Q^(1)_plmn and Q^(2)_plmn of Eq. (7) for a step-index fiber, a cylindrically symmetric fiber of arbitrary profile, and a hexagonally symmetric (C6v) microstructured fiber. This deck reproduces the step-index case: the weakly-guiding LP mode set of the paper's Fig. 1 fiber, the overlap integrals Eq. (7) evaluated from first principles, and the spatial selection rules Eq. (18), the polarisation selection rules Eq. (19), the permutation identities Eq. (16), the real-basis statement Q^(1) = Q^(2) of Sec. 3, and the Section 5 complexity argument built on the number of surviving coefficients. The polarisation-closure consequence (a single circular polarisation stays closed, Sec. 3.B / Eq. 14) is then exercised on the library engine.

fiber.page_ref: paper p. 1649 (Fig. 1 caption): 'a step-index fiber with a 6 um core radius and numerical aperture (NA) = 0.17 at 1.5 um'

mode_set.LP31_cutoff: j_{2,1} = 5.5206 > V, so no higher azimuthal family is guided
mode_set.counting: LP01 gives 2 modes (sigma = +/-), LP11 and LP21 give 4 each (helical m = +/-1, +/-2 crossed with sigma = +/-): 2 + 4 + 4 = 10
mode_set.why_ten: the paper's Fig. 1 uses 'the first ten modes', giving 2 x 10^4 = 20000 coefficients for the two types of Eq. (7) -- the same count this set gives
mode_set.basis_helical: F_p(r, phi) = R_p(r) exp(i m_p phi) (paper Eq. 17); the basis in which Eq. (18) is written
mode_set.basis_real: the physical LP basis, R(r) cos(m phi) and R(r) sin(m phi) (one shape for m = 0); used for the Q^(1) = Q^(2) statement of Sec. 3 and for the engine deck
mode_set.normalisation: N_k = INT |F_k|^2 dx dy = 1 for every mode, so Eq. (7)'s 1/(N_p N_l N_m N_n) is unity; tensors are reported divided by Q^(typ)_0000
mode_set.solver: analytic step-index LP eigenvalue equation u J_{l-1}(u)/J_l(u) + w K_{l+1}(w)/K_l(w) = 2l with w = sqrt(V^2 - u^2), bisected by scipy.optimize.brentq
mode_set.quadrature: polar grid, 601 points linear in the core (r = 1 is a grid point) + 1400 log-spaced points to r = 20, 256 azimuthal points; trapezoidal weights

eq18_spatial_selection.how_measured: the angular factor is evaluated by quadrature, not hard-coded, so the rule EMERGES from Eq. (7); the residual |Q| over the forbidden quadruples must be at round-off

eq19_polarisation_selection.rule: Q^(typ)_plmn = 0 for sigma_p != sigma_l or sigma_m != sigma_n
eq19_polarisation_selection.basis_reason: with F = R(r) a(phi) e_sigma and e_+/e_- = (ex +/- i ey)/sqrt(2), the Cartesian dot product e_{sigma_p}* . e_{sigma_l} = delta is an exact identity of the circular basis
eq19_polarisation_selection.consequence: all four-wave-mixing terms between e_+ and e_- vanish: a pulse launched in a single circular polarisation stays in it (paper Sec. 3.B, Eq. 14)

checked_results.sec3_real_basis: for real-valued mode functions F_l* = F_l, so the two integrands of Eq. (7) coincide and Q^(1) = Q^(2) element-wise; this holds exactly in the real (cos/sin) LP basis and fails in the helical Eq. (17) basis
checked_results.sec5_complexity: the three-term product of Eq. (6) scales as O(M^4 N) if no constraints are imposed on Q; the selection rules cut the surviving coefficient count by the factor reported in the deck output

paper_fig1_numbers.note: the paper evaluates these with the EXACT complex-valued vectorial mode functions of a step-index fiber. The weakly-guiding scalar model implemented here does not reproduce these two counts (it gives 8640 zeros per type from the spatial rule alone, and no surviving coefficient below 1 % of the maximum). Reproducing 17872/936 needs a full vectorial HE/EH/TE/TM mode solver, which is out of scope for this deck; the qualitative reading of Fig. 1 (a log-log distribution with a plateau and a small-coefficient tail) is reproduced. Recorded as a caveat in the folder README.

engine_deck.xpm_weights: Q^(1)_{i i j j} of the real LP basis (diagonal = SPM, off-diagonal = the physical inter-modal Kerr coefficient)
engine_deck.fwm_weights: Q^(2)_{m n n q}, the degenerate (pump-driven) slice the engine's A_n^2 A_q* FWM term implements; the non-degenerate arms l != p of Eq. (6) are outside the engine's scalar-channel geometry
engine_deck.oam_gate: the engine's oam_l gate l_m = l_n + l_p - l_q on its (m, n, n, q) slice is the type-2 rule Eq. (18) read with (p, l, m, n) = (n, n, m, q), which reduces to m_m + m_q = 2 m_n; asserted algebraically on the helical tensor
engine_deck.raman_reason: the delayed Raman term of Eq. (6) breaks the per-mode energy conservation Eq. (15) by design (the paper says so explicitly), so the conservation check runs with R' = delta(t)
engine_deck.run_a: 10 channels (the full paper Fig. 1 mode set), XPM only, one Gaussian per sigma = + channel, L = 2 m
engine_deck.run_b: 4 channels (LP01+/-, LP11 cos +/-) with include_fwm and pump depletion, plus an isotropic-weight control that must leak
